welcome.title: Welcome to Kinstamp
welcome.body: USCIS is a public board: anyone with a receipt number can read a case's status there, and it never shows personal data. Kinstamp is your private notebook on top of it: which cases you follow, what you call them, the dates you note, who you share with. Only you see your notebook.

caseCard.body: Each card shows the current status and the last change. Tap a case to open it.

insights.title: Insights
insights.body: How long cases like yours take, computed from anonymous data and only from people who gave consent.

account.title: Your account

keyDates.title: Key dates

plain.title: In plain language
plain.disclaimer: General information based on the status category. It is not legal advice.

received.meaning: USCIS has your filing and assigned it a receipt number. Nothing is needed from you right now.

next.1: A biometrics appointment notice, if your form requires fingerprints.
next.2: Weeks or months of waiting while the case sits in the queue for its form type.
next.3: A request for evidence or a decision.

biometrics.meaning: USCIS scheduled or completed the collection of your fingerprints and photo.

next.1: Attend the appointment on the notice, or wait for the results if it already happened.
next.2: Background checks run in the background; no action is needed.
next.3: The case moves to review by an officer.

interview.meaning: An officer wants to see you in person. The notice gives the date, place and what to bring.

next.1: Prepare the documents listed on the notice.
next.2: Attend the interview; your attorney may accompany you.
next.3: A decision, sometimes the same day, sometimes weeks later.

evidence_requested.meaning: USCIS needs more documents before deciding. The notice lists exactly what is missing and the deadline to respond.

next.1: Gather everything the notice asks for; send it in one package before the deadline.
next.2: USCIS confirms it received your response.
next.3: The case goes back to review and then to a decision.

evidence_received.meaning: USCIS received the documents you sent in response to its request.

next.1: An officer reviews the new evidence.
next.2: A decision, or in rare cases another request.

approved.meaning: USCIS approved your filing. An approval notice is on its way or already with you.

next.1: Keep the approval notice; it is proof of the decision.
next.2: If a card is involved, USCIS produces and mails it next.
next.3: Check whether a next step depends on this approval, for example a visa interview or a new filing.

card_produced.meaning: USCIS produced your card and it is on its way by mail.

next.1: Expect the card by mail within a couple of weeks.
next.2: A tracking number may appear on the USCIS case status page.

card_delivered.meaning: The post office reports that your card was delivered.

next.1: Check that the details on the card are correct.
next.2: Contact USCIS if the card did not arrive.

transferred.meaning: USCIS moved your case to a different office to balance workloads. It does not restart the process.

next.1: A notice from the new office with its address.
next.2: Processing continues from where it was.

denied.meaning: USCIS denied the filing. The notice explains the reasons and whether you can appeal or file a motion.

next.1: Read the denial notice carefully and note any deadline.
next.2: Talk to an attorney about options such as an appeal, a motion to reopen or a new filing.

withdrawn.meaning: The filing was withdrawn, so USCIS will not decide on it.

next.1: If this was not intended, contact USCIS or your attorney.

other.meaning: USCIS gave this case a status we don't have a plain-language explanation for yet. The full USCIS text above is the best source.

next.1: Keep checking: Kinstamp records every change with its date.

privacy.title: Your data stays yours.
privacy.public: USCIS's case status page is public and shows no personal data: anyone with a receipt number reads the same status.
privacy.private: Kinstamp is your family's private notebook on top of it: which cases you track, their nicknames, key dates and who you share with, protected by row-level security in the database. Anonymous insights come only from people who opt in, and only for groups of 5 or more cases.
